invariant_argument: Each explicit From body is exactly one matching enum constructor, retaining its entire owned defect. Rust enum constructors preserve fields and discriminate wrappers; no arithmetic, narrowing, search or exception suppression occurs.

All thiserror attributes were read against all 23 variants: three transparent provider wrappers, four prefixed domain wrappers, one matrix #[from] source wrapper and 15 local field-bearing diagnostics. Native challenges instantiate all variants, all eight From conversions, field-rich payloads, maximum-u128 display, clone/equality and explicit source behavior.

Direct conversions are constant work and allocate nothing; Display/Clone delegate payload-dependent work. Arbitrary string length and provider formatting/clone costs are outside an allocator or runtime guarantee. The enum is forgeable data and never treated as a mathematical certificate.

trust_boundary: Rust enum/derive semantics, pinned thiserror proc macro and actual wrapped provider error implementations. Display/Clone/source behavior of providers is trusted and content-bound. No catch-all conversion or recovery is introduced.
consumer_review: All actual fusion modules use this shared nominal enum, including typed ? conversions from native exact-field/matrix/scalar providers. The native fixtures compile whole packages, preserving nominal type composition; both canonical roots replay against the same source.
Constructors accept arbitrary witness values; consumers must establish the underlying failure condition. Diagnostic data alone authorizes no proof/score promotion.
assurance_limits: AuthorityEffect: None. This L1 utility preserves diagnostics; it does not establish whether a reported defect holds.

Derive-generated bodies are explicitly audited and native-challenged; the AST metric counts the four authored conversion bodies only. No compiler expansion theorem, provider-wide safety grade or general crash-freedom theorem is claimed.
